# sandbox

Runs the Flamingo node somewhere isolated from the machine it runs on, and nothing above
this module needs to know where that is. Today it is Docker. That is the only place in
flamingo-node that knows.

```js
const sandbox = require('sandbox')

await sandbox.up(app)   // app is the flamingo-node folder
await sandbox.running()
await sandbox.logs()
await sandbox.down()
```

| Function | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `up(app)` | Make sure the sandbox runtime is installed, prepare the node and start it. Returns once it is started; the services inside it keep coming up. Refuses if it is already running. |
| `running()` | Whether the node is up. |
| `logs()` | Follow its output in this terminal until Ctrl+C. |
| `down()` | Stop bitcoind and the lightning nodes cleanly, then take the node down. Waits for each one to exit, so nothing is killed mid write. |

## How it works today

- **Docker.** `install.js` checks `docker --version` and installs Docker if it is missing
  (`get.docker.com` on linux and macOS, winget on Windows). Docker has to be available for
  any of this to work.
- **The image** is built from the `Dockerfile` in the
  [flamingo-docker](https://github.com/basim-12/flamingo-docker) dependency, pinned to a
  commit in flamingo-node's `package.json`, so the same commit always produces the same
  image.
- **The container** is started with `docker run`, with its arguments read from that
  dependency's `docker-compose.json`: the volumes it mounts (the flamingo-node folder, the
  data folder, `env.docker.json`), the ports it publishes and the command it runs. We read
  the compose file ourselves rather than calling `docker compose`, so there is one way the
  node starts and no second tool in the middle. `${FLAMINGO_PATH}` in a volume resolves to
  the `app` folder passed to `up()`.
- **Stopping** is deliberate rather than a `docker stop`: each lightning node is stopped
  over its RPC and waited for, then bitcoind the same way, and only then is the container
  removed. A lightning node killed mid write can lose channel state.
- **`exec.js`** wraps `spawn` and `spawnSync` in promises. `bare-subprocess` has no `exec`,
  `execFile` or `execSync`, so everything here is spawn based and reads output as bytes.
- **Both runtimes.** This module loads under Node and under Bare. Its `package.json`
  `imports` map points `child_process`, `fs`, `os` and `path` at the `bare-*` packages when
  Bare resolves them, and Node ignores the map because its keys do not start with `#`.

## Replacing Docker

Everything above this module talks to `up` / `down` / `running` / `logs` and never names
Docker, a container or an image, so another sandbox can take its place without changing
anything else. What a drive would declare for itself, rather than inheriting one prepared
image, is sketched in [scripts/kits.md](../../../scripts/kits.md).
